title: Mishnah Berurah — Wikisource
attribution: Mishnah Berurah by Rabbi Israel Meir HaKohen of Radin; transcription and edits by Hebrew Wikisource contributors. The source manifest gives a revision and contributor-history link for each siman.
changes: Extracted text from revision-specific rendered Wikisource pages, grouped commentary by its labelled Shulchan Arukh seif or the only seif of an unheaded siman, and removed page navigation and headings. Six misdirected heading links in simanim 49, 91 and 128 were checked against Sefaria passage links (CC BY 4.0). Siman 509 text embedded on the siman 508 page is kept only under its matching 509 source. Copyrightable adaptations are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0. No OCR or new translation was performed by Amudi; the historical digitization method is not established.
coverageStatus: Partial Hebrew source edition: labelled sections and single-seif siman passages from Wikisource simanim 1–697; ambiguous headings, unverified pages and separate unplaced sections are omitted.

alignment: Headings explicitly naming a seif on the same siman page, with no contradictory link, are mapped to a populated seif in the source-checked Lemberg edition. Six erroneous heading links in simanim 49, 91 and 128 were checked against the section headings, every numbered comment, Sefaria links and the base text. If an unheaded source page has a single populated base seif, its paragraphs are associated with that seif and identified separately. Material embedded from another siman is excluded here and retained under the target page only when the section is identical. Each full source section is grouped as one item; individual subcomment word offsets are not asserted.
